slides.0.title: Côte-Rôtie, Condrieu and Château-Grillet
slides.0.subtitle: The far north of the Rhône
slides.1.title: Côte-Rôtie: the roasted slope
slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOC and area
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Recognised by decree on 18 October 1940; red wine only. Located in the Ampuis, Saint-Cyr-sur-le-Rhône and Tupin-et-Semons communes of the Rhône département. About 342 ha in 2025 (Inter Rhône)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: At least 80% Syrah, Viognier allowed
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Syrah must be at least 80% of both plantings and blend; Viognier, the accessory variety, may be interplanted with Syrah up to 20% of the vines in a Syrah plot, and is often co-fermented with it
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Yield and density
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Yield 40 hl/ha (ceiling 46; above 60 the whole harvest loses the AOC); minimum natural alcohol 10.5%; at least 6,000 vines per hectare
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Côte Blonde and Côte Brune
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The specification names both: Côte Blonde on gneiss with lighter siliceous soils; Côte Brune on mica-schist with darker, iron-rich clayey soils
slides.1.content: Côte-Rôtie keywords: Syrah ≥80%, Viognier ≤20%, co-fermentation, two slopes.
slides.2.title: Viticulture and style in Côte-Rôtie
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Steep terraces
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Vines grow on steep terraces, traditionally staked (échalas) and held by dry-stone walls (chaillées), worked almost entirely by hand
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Why co-ferment (common view)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: It is commonly said that co-fermenting with Viognier lifts the aromatics and helps stabilise colour; this is a style explanation, not a rule, and is not tested
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Famous single vineyards (common)
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Guigal's La Mouline (Côte Blonde), La Landonne and La Turque (Côte Brune) and similar single vineyards made Côte-Rôtie famous
slides.2.highlights.3.title: The labour of the slopes
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Bourgogne Aujourd'hui (2026) notes the documentary Les Chaillées de l'Enfer, following work on the slopes at Georges Vernay between Condrieu and Côte-Rôtie
slides.2.content: Style notes are common wisdom; for rules questions just remember 80/20 and the two slopes.
slides.3.title: Condrieu: home of Viognier
slides.3.highlights.0.title: AOC and area
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Recognised by decree on 27 April 1940 (originally still white only); seven communes: Condrieu (Rhône), Limony (Ardèche) and Chavanay, Malleval, Saint-Michel-sur-Rhône, Saint-Pierre-de-Bœuf and Vérin (Loire). About 216 ha in 2025
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Viognier only
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The specification allows wine only from Viognier (100%); yield 41 hl/ha (ceiling 46); minimum natural alcohol 11.5%
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Styles
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Mainly dry; in suitable years overripe grapes yield a little moelleux or doux, and the label must say demi-sec, moelleux or doux when the wine is not sec. The draft specification does not mention sparkling wine
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Soils
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Granite terraces; CMS materials call Condrieu's thin, mica-rich weathered topsoil arzelle and the bare granite of Cornas gore
slides.3.content: Condrieu is a 100% Viognier white AOC spread over seven communes in three départements.
slides.4.title: Château-Grillet: a single-estate AOC
slides.4.highlights.0.title: AOC and location
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Recognised in 1936 (INAO text: granted 8 December, published 11 December); in Saint-Michel-sur-Rhône and Vérin (Loire), enclosed by the Condrieu area
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Viognier and size
slides.4.highlights.1.content: The only variety is Viognier, white only; the text says "fewer than 3.5 ha in production" and Inter Rhône 2025 shows 4 ha — one of France's smallest AOCs
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Ownership
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Long held as a monopoly by the Neyret-Gachet family (the INAO text says since 1830); Decanter reported in 2011 that François Pinault bought the estate
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Ageing
slides.4.highlights.3.content: The text describes a dry wine aged partly in oak barrels for at least 18 months (descriptive wording, not tested)
slides.4.content: A monopole AOC: the whole appellation belongs to a single producer.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What is the minimum share of Syrah required in Côte-Rôtie?
At least 80% Syrah; Viognier may account for at most 20% of the vines in Syrah plots.
What characterises the soils of the Côte Brune?
A. Gneiss and lighter siliceous soil
B. Mica-schist and darker, iron-rich clayey soil
The Côte Brune has mica-schist and darker iron-rich clay; the Côte Blonde has gneiss and lighter siliceous soils.
Which grape does Condrieu's specification permit?
What kind of AOC is Château-Grillet?
A. A large appellation of dozens of communes
Château-Grillet is only about 4 ha, with the whole AOC belonging to one producer, making Viognier white only.
